title: World Youth Championships day seven preview: Wen Ruibo meets Hung Che-Yen again as China chase both doubles titles
seo_title: World Youth Championships day 7 preview and UK times
description: World Youth Championships day seven: U19 singles quarter-finals, including Li Hechen v Emanuel Otalvaro, and both doubles finals in Istanbul, in UK time.
standfirst: Li Hechen gets another chance against Emanuel Otalvaro, who beat him at the Youth Olympic Games, before Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi play for their third gold medals of the week.
body: China can win both under-19 doubles titles at the World Youth Championships in Istanbul on Friday, and all four of their players are in the singles quarter-finals, which start at 11am UK time.

Eight singles quarter-finals, four boys' and four girls', are played in pairs from 11am to about 2pm UK time. South Korea's Jeong Yein and Heo Yerim play Jiang Yiyi and Yao Ruixuan in the girls' doubles final at about 4pm, and Wen Ruibo and Li Hechen meet Kim Daehwan and Lee Hyeonho in the boys' final at about 4.30pm. Wen and Jiang, already team and mixed doubles champions, can leave with four golds each.
## The big matches
**Wen Ruibo v Hung Che-Yen (11am UK)**

This is a rematch of the match that settled Monday's boys' team final. Hung, 17 and ranked 128th, had beaten Li in the opening match of that final, and he came back from two games down against Wen before the world No 14 won the decider 11-2. Wen, 19, has dropped 33 points in two singles matches here; Hung lost the first game to Turkey's Kenan Kahraman in the last 16 and won the next four.
**Li Hechen v Emanuel Otalvaro (11.45am UK)**

The Dakar rematch. Otalvaro, Colombia's 16-year-old second seed, beat Li 4-1 in the boys' singles quarter-finals at the [Youth Olympic Games](/news/youth-olympic-games-dakar-2026-otalvaro-beats-li-hechen-china-no-medal.html) this month, the result that left China without a table tennis medal at the Games for the first time. He went on to win silver. Otalvaro, ranked 106th, swept India's Priyanuj Bhattacharyya on Thursday, while Li, 17, the sixth seed and world No 177, dropped a game to Italy's Francesco Trevisan.
**Jiang Yiyi v Wu Ying Syuan (12.30pm UK)**

Jiang, the girls' top seed and world No 188, turned 16 last week and beat Takamori and Yuna Ojio in Monday's team final. Wu, 17, Taiwan's fifth seed and the world No 163, beat Romania's Bianca Mei-Rosu in five games after losing the fourth 11-5.
**Divyanshi Bhowmick v Hana Goda (1.15pm UK)**

Goda, 18, is the world No 21 and the highest-ranked woman in Istanbul. The Egyptian third seed has dropped 41 points in two matches. Bhowmick, India's eighth seed, who turned 16 on 19 November and is ranked 100th, needed seven games against Poland's Natalia Bogdanowicz on Thursday, winning the decider 11-5 after losing the fifth and sixth.
## Two Indians and two French players

India have two girls in the last eight. Syndrela Das, 17 and the world No 95, beat the seventh seed Sally Moyland and then the ninth seed Wu Jia-En, the second of them 11-9 in the seventh game after 55 minutes. She opens the day against Japan's second seed Mao Takamori, 18, who beat Yao in Monday's team final.

France's Leana Hochart, 18 and ranked 227th, knocked out Hong Kong's fourth seed Su Tsz Tung and now plays Yao, the sixth seed. Yao, 17, came from three games down against Russia's Eseniia Shirokova on Thursday. In the boys' draw Antoine Noirault, 19 and ranked 254th, beat Hong Kong's fourth seed Li Ki Ho and plays Australia's Aditya Sareen, 18 and ranked 112th, who came from 3-1 down against Taiwan's seventh seed Lin Chin-Ting in the last 32. Noirault and Hochart both won doubles bronze on Thursday.
Japan's Shunto Iwaida, 17 and ranked 416th, has not dropped a game in the singles and plays Tunisia's Wassim Essid, 18 and the world No 130, who has needed 12 games to win his two matches.
## The doubles finals

Jeong, 18, and Heo, 16, the girls' top seeds, beat Hochart and Alexia Nodin in four games in the semi-finals. Jiang and Yao lost the first two games of theirs 13-11 and 14-12 to Takamori and Aoba Takahashi before winning the next three.
Wen and Li dropped 15 points against Nathan Pilard and Noirault. Kim and Lee, both 16 and seeded 12th, beat the third seeds, Alan Kurmangaliyev and Benyamin Faraji, 11-6, 11-6, 11-5.
## Order of play
Times are approximate and UK time (Istanbul is three hours ahead). Seeds in brackets.

- 11am: Wen Ruibo (CHN, 1) v Hung Che-Yen (TPE, 12); Syndrela Das (IND) v Mao Takamori (JPN, 2)
- 11.45am: Leana Hochart (FRA, 15) v Yao Ruixuan (CHN, 6); Li Hechen (CHN, 6) v Emanuel Otalvaro (COL, 2)
- 12.30pm: Shunto Iwaida (JPN, 13) v Wassim Essid (TUN); Jiang Yiyi (CHN, 1) v Wu Ying Syuan (TPE, 5)
- 1.15pm: Divyanshi Bhowmick (IND, 8) v Hana Goda (EGY, 3); Antoine Noirault (FRA) v Aditya Sareen (AUS)
- 4pm: girls' doubles final, Jeong Yein / Heo Yerim (KOR, 1) v Jiang Yiyi / Yao Ruixuan (CHN, 2)
- 4.30pm: boys' doubles final, Wen Ruibo / Li Hechen (CHN, 1) v Kim Daehwan / Lee Hyeonho (KOR, 12)
## How to watch

Eleven's [event page](/events/world-youth-championships-2026.html#matches) has live scores, the full draws and the order of play, and shows the stream whenever one is live. The singles are best of seven games and the doubles best of five. The semi-finals are on Saturday from about 8.30am UK time, with the two finals later that day, the last of the championships.
## Thursday in brief

Wen and Jiang beat Li and Yao 4-11, 11-4, 11-6, 11-4 in the mixed doubles final. The details are in Eleven's [day six review](/news/world-youth-championships-2026-day-six-review-results-highlights.html).
